values.title: History
values.body:
Four decades on 5th Avenue

RES opened in 1982 as a twelve-table neighborhood bar. The room has grown, but the welcome has not changed.

RES Bar & Restaurant at a glance:

  • Seasonal American kitchen and bar
  • 4 5th Avenue at St. Marks Place, Cathedral District Brooklyn, NY 11217
  • Established 1982

From the chalkboard menu of our first year to the wood-fired kitchen of today, RES has always been a place for the neighborhood: somewhere to celebrate, to catch up with friends or simply to enjoy a good meal after work. Many of our regulars have been coming for decades, and some of our cooks started here as dishwashers. We are proud of that history, and we are still writing it every night.

values.title: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service
values.excerpt: Great food brings guests in the first time; great service is what brings them back. After four decades on 5th Avenue, these are the four habits our floor team practises every single shift.
values.body:
Great food brings guests in the first time; great service is what brings them back. After four decades on 5th Avenue, these are the four habits our floor team practises every single shift.

Greet every table within a minute. Even on the busiest Friday night, a quick hello and a glass of water tells guests they have been seen. The order can wait a moment; the welcome cannot.

Know the menu like a cook. Our servers taste every new dish before it goes on the menu, so they can explain what is in it, how it is cooked and what to drink with it, and answer allergy questions with confidence.

Listen more than you talk, and close the loop. When something is not right we fix it at the table, then tell the kitchen so it does not happen again. A complaint handled well often turns a guest into a regular.

values.title: Chipotle to launch burger spinoff this fall
values.excerpt: Fast-casual chains keep testing new concepts, and a burger spinoff from a burrito brand is the latest sign that the category is still hungry for growth.
values.body:
Fast-casual chains keep testing new concepts, and a burger spinoff from a burrito brand is the latest sign that the category is still hungry for growth.

For neighborhood restaurants the lesson is not to chase the trend but to understand what guests are asking for: fresh ingredients, a short menu they can trust and food that arrives quickly without tasting rushed.

Our own burger has been on the menu since 1982. We grind the beef in-house every morning, toast the buns to order and keep the toppings simple. Sometimes the best answer to a new trend is to keep doing one thing very well.

values.title: How To Help Your Chef Achieve A Better Work-Life Balance
values.excerpt: Kitchens are famous for long hours and little rest. Keeping a talented chef means taking their time off as seriously as their time on the line.
values.body:
Kitchens are famous for long hours and little rest. Keeping a talented chef means taking their time off as seriously as their time on the line.

At RES we plan the rota four weeks ahead, give every cook two consecutive days off and close the kitchen for a full week each January. Prep lists are shared so no one person carries the whole service, and the sous chef runs the pass two nights a week so the head chef can go home to their family.

The result is a calmer kitchen, fewer mistakes and a team that has stayed with us for years. Guests may never see it, but they taste it in every plate.

values.title: Indies aren't sold on tech
values.excerpt: Independent restaurants are being offered more apps, tablets and dashboards than ever, yet many owners remain unconvinced that every new screen makes the dining room better.
values.body:
Independent restaurants are being offered more apps, tablets and dashboards than ever, yet many owners remain unconvinced that every new screen makes the dining room better.

Technology earns its place when it saves time for the team or makes life easier for the guest: online reservations, a reliable card terminal at the table, a kitchen display that keeps tickets in order. It loses its place when it gets between the server and the guest.

We use a simple booking system and a kitchen printer that has not missed a ticket in years. Everything else we judge by one question: does it help us look after the people in front of us?

values.title: Starbucks brings Under Armour exec on board
values.excerpt: When a coffee giant hires an executive from a sportswear brand, it is a reminder that restaurant brands are as much about experience and loyalty as they are about the product in the cup.
values.body:
When a coffee giant hires an executive from a sportswear brand, it is a reminder that restaurant brands are as much about experience and loyalty as they are about the product in the cup.

Big chains borrow ideas from retail: loyalty programmes, mobile ordering and carefully designed stores. Small restaurants can borrow too, at a human scale. Remembering a regular’s usual order is still the best loyalty programme there is.

At RES our bartenders know hundreds of guests by name and by drink. No app can replace that, but it is worth watching how the big players think about the whole journey from the front door to the last sip.

values.title: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus
values.excerpt: Ideas that start in fine-dining kitchens tend to reach everyday menus a few years later. Here are eight we are seeing on menus across the country, and in our own kitchen.
values.body:
Ideas that start in fine-dining kitchens tend to reach everyday menus a few years later. Here are eight we are seeing on menus across the country, and in our own kitchen.

1. Vegetables as the main course, not the side. 2. Fermentation: house pickles, kimchi and hot sauces. 3. Wood-fired cooking for smoke and char. 4. Smaller plates made for sharing.

5. Global breakfast dishes served all day. 6. Low- and no-alcohol cocktails with as much care as the classics. 7. Heritage grains in breads and salads. 8. Menus that name the farms and fishermen behind each dish.

Not every trend belongs on every menu. We keep the ones that make our food taste better and leave the rest to others.

values.title: Starbucks faces a big recall
values.excerpt: A product recall at a chain the size of Starbucks makes headlines, but the way a business responds matters just as much to every restaurant, large or small.
values.body:
A product recall at a chain the size of Starbucks makes headlines, but the way a business responds matters just as much to every restaurant, large or small.

Food safety starts long before anything reaches the table: trusted suppliers, clear labelling, cold chains that are checked and logged, and a team trained to raise a concern the moment something looks wrong.

In our kitchen every delivery is checked on arrival, every container is dated and every allergen is written on the prep sheet. If something ever goes wrong, we tell our guests quickly and honestly. That is how trust is kept.

values.title: Logan's said to be weighing bankruptcy
values.excerpt: Reports that a casual-dining chain may be weighing bankruptcy are a sign of how hard the middle of the market has become, squeezed between fast-casual prices and fine-dining experiences.
values.body:
Reports that a casual-dining chain may be weighing bankruptcy are a sign of how hard the middle of the market has become, squeezed between fast-casual prices and fine-dining experiences.

Rising food and labour costs, rent and changing habits hit every restaurant. The ones that last tend to know exactly who they are cooking for, keep their menus focused and invest in the people who run the dining room.

We have been through a few difficult years since 1982. Each time, the answer was the same: listen to our regulars, keep the quality up and never stop giving people a reason to come back.

values.title: Fish sauces seep onto all sorts of menus
values.excerpt: Once found mostly in Southeast Asian kitchens, fish sauce is now turning up in salad dressings, marinades, burgers and even cocktails.
values.body:
Once found mostly in Southeast Asian kitchens, fish sauce is now turning up in salad dressings, marinades, burgers and even cocktails.

A few drops add a deep, savoury note that is hard to place but easy to love. Our chefs use it in the glaze for our chili chicken, in the dressing for the grilled romaine salad and in a slow-cooked tomato sauce that tastes richer than its three ingredients.

The trick is balance: a little acid, a little sweetness and a light hand. Used well, fish sauce does not taste of fish at all; it simply makes everything around it taste more like itself.

values.title: Denny’s adopts a pancake guarantee
values.excerpt: A pancake guarantee is a bold promise: if the stack is not right, it is on the house. It is also a smart way to show confidence in a signature dish.
values.body:
A pancake guarantee is a bold promise: if the stack is not right, it is on the house. It is also a smart way to show confidence in a signature dish.

Guarantees work when the kitchen can deliver them every time. That means a tested recipe, consistent equipment and cooks who know what "right" looks like.

Our own weekend brunch has a quieter promise. If anything on your plate is not as you expected, tell your server and we will make it again. It rarely happens, and when it does, it helps us get better.

values.title: BLT on Pimento Cheese Biscuit
values.excerpt: Our brunch menu has a new favourite: a classic BLT built on a warm, flaky pimento cheese biscuit.
values.body:
Our brunch menu has a new favourite: a classic BLT built on a warm, flaky pimento cheese biscuit.

We bake the biscuits every morning with sharp cheddar, roasted red peppers and a pinch of cayenne, then split them and layer thick-cut smoked bacon, crisp lettuce and ripe tomato with a smear of house mayonnaise.

It is served with a side of pickled vegetables and a choice of fries or salad, Saturdays and Sundays from 10 am. Come early; the biscuits usually sell out before noon.

values.title: McDonald’s makes 'clean' tweaks to some menu items
values.excerpt: Big burger chains are simplifying ingredient lists, removing artificial preservatives and colours from some of their best-known items.
values.body:
Big burger chains are simplifying ingredient lists, removing artificial preservatives and colours from some of their best-known items.

Guests increasingly want to know what is in their food and where it comes from. That is good news for everyone who cooks from scratch.

At RES our sauces, dressings and stocks are made in-house, and our servers can tell you exactly what goes into every dish. "Clean" was never a trend for us; it is simply how a good kitchen works.

values.title: How the GOP and Dems differ on restaurant issues
values.excerpt: Minimum wage, tipping, tax credits and health rules: restaurant owners follow policy debates closely because the outcomes land directly on their payroll and their menus.
values.body:
Minimum wage, tipping, tax credits and health rules: restaurant owners follow policy debates closely because the outcomes land directly on their payroll and their menus.

Whatever the politics, the questions every restaurant faces are practical ones. How do we pay our team fairly and keep prices our guests can afford? How do we plan when the rules may change next year?

We believe the answers start at home: transparent pay, clear communication with our staff and guests, and staying involved with the local business associations that speak for independent restaurants in Brooklyn.

values.title: Chefs
values.body:
Our kitchen is led by a small team of cooks who have worked together for years. They share one rule: every plate that leaves the pass should be one they would be proud to eat themselves.

Each season the team tastes, tests and argues over the new menu until every dish earns its place. Come and meet them at the chef’s counter, where you can watch dinner being cooked over the wood fire.

items.title: Discover Our Story
items.description: RES opened its doors on 5th Avenue in 1982 as a twelve-table neighborhood bar with a short menu and a long wine list. Four decades later the room is bigger and the kitchen busier, but the idea is the same: honest food cooked from scratch, drinks poured generously and a dining room where regulars and first-timers are greeted the same way. Many of our suppliers have been with us for more than twenty years, and our recipes still start with what the farmers bring in each morning.

items.title: premium food experience
items.description: Our chefs build every plate around the season: spring peas and ramps, summer tomatoes, autumn squash and slow braises through the winter. Breads are baked in-house every morning, pasta is rolled by hand and fish arrives daily from the Fulton market. Pair it with a cocktail from the bar or a bottle from our cellar, and let our team take care of the rest.

values.title: Our Team

items.member_desc: Dewey has led the RES kitchen for over a decade, cooking seasonal plates built on produce from farms across the Hudson Valley.
Lorenzo runs the line every night and brings the flavours of his family’s trattoria to our pasta and wood-fired dishes.
Perry bakes our bread each morning and is the reason guests save room for tiramisu and warm chocolate lava cake.
Darren looks after the bar, from classic cocktails to the local craft beers that rotate on our taps every week.

items.title: A new chapter for the dining room

items.description: RES opened as a twelve-table neighborhood bar at 4 5th Avenue, serving a short menu of home-style plates and local beer to the people of Brooklyn. The first menu was written on a chalkboard, and it still hangs by the door.
